Well it depends on what you're doing and for how long.

Most of the times I've camped off a trail I was backpacking with friends. If the weather might be rainy, cold, or just questionable we'd take a tent. Since tents can be heavy we'd divide up the pieces and each carry part of it. As far as food goes we'd usually pack stuff that can be carried easily and relatively lightweight. You'll want to make sure you take plenty of water and it's also preferable to try to camp near a water source. If it's running water like a stream, you can purify your own water and cut down on some of the weight you have to carry. If you're going to be backpacking avoid the beer. It's heavy to carry and you do not want it in your system when hiking. As far as a fire goes, depending on where you camp, you can probably make a small fire sufficient for your needs. If you make a fire, make sure to check whether you can cut down limbs or trees for firewood. A lot of state and national parks don't allow that and it's probably better anyway to just find your firewood on the ground. I've seen people recommend fancy gadgets for starting a fire but a simple bic lighter works fine. Even if it gets wet it will still light when it dries out.

If you're just pulling the car up to a place that isn't a traditional campsite, you can probably get away with bringing whatever you usually bring to a campsite. Probably the most important part people forget when camping off trail or in a non-traditional campsite is to clean up after themselves. When you leave, there should be little to no evidence that someone camped there; pick up your trash, don't cut down trees or limbs, and put out your fires thoroughly and scatter the ashes. People who don't clean up after themselves don't really have much respect for the trail they're camping on or the other people using that trail.
